# Regression Accelerated Bayesian Additive Regression Trees Learner

Accelerated Bayesian additive regression trees (XBART) for regression.
Calls [`XBART::XBART()`](https://rdrr.io/pkg/XBART/man/XBART.html) from
package 'XBART'.

The prediction is the mean over the sweeps after the burn-in period, as
recommended by the upstream package. XBART draws random numbers from its
own generator and ignores
[`set.seed()`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/Random.html). Set the
`random_seed` parameter to obtain reproducible results. Messages printed
by XBART during training are suppressed unless `verbose` is `TRUE`.

## Installation

Package 'XBART' is not on CRAN and has to be installed from GitHub via
`remotes::install_github("JingyuHe/XBART")`. Compiling it requires the
GNU Scientific Library (GSL) and the Boost headers, e.g. via
`apt install libgsl-dev libboost-dev` or `brew install gsl boost`.

## Initial parameter values

- `num_trees` is initialized to 100 and `num_sweeps` to 40, because
  [`XBART::XBART()`](https://rdrr.io/pkg/XBART/man/XBART.html) has no
  defaults for them.

- `nthread` is initialized to 1 to avoid conflicts with parallelization
  via [future](https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=future).

## Dictionary

This [Learner](https://mlr3.mlr-org.com/reference/Learner.html) can be
instantiated via
[lrn()](https://mlr3.mlr-org.com/reference/mlr_sugar.html):

    lrn("regr.xbart")

## Meta Information

- Task type: “regr”

- Predict Types: “response”

- Feature Types: “logical”, “integer”, “numeric”

- Required Packages: [mlr3](https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=mlr3),
  [mlr3extralearners](https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=mlr3extralearners),
  [XBART](https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=XBART)

## Parameters

|                  |         |         |             |                       |
|------------------|---------|---------|-------------|-----------------------|
| Id               | Type    | Default | Levels      | Range                 |
| num_trees        | integer | \-      |             | \\\[1, \infty)\\      |
| num_sweeps       | integer | \-      |             | \\\[1, \infty)\\      |
| max_depth        | integer | 250     |             | \\\[1, \infty)\\      |
| Nmin             | integer | 1       |             | \\\[1, \infty)\\      |
| num_cutpoints    | integer | 100     |             | \\\[1, \infty)\\      |
| alpha            | numeric | 0.95    |             | \\\[0, 1\]\\          |
| beta             | numeric | 1.25    |             | \\\[0, \infty)\\      |
| tau              | numeric | \-      |             | \\\[0, \infty)\\      |
| no_split_penalty | numeric | \-      |             | \\\[0, \infty)\\      |
| burnin           | integer | 1       |             | \\\[0, \infty)\\      |
| mtry             | integer | \-      |             | \\\[1, \infty)\\      |
| p_categorical    | integer | 0       |             | \\\[0, \infty)\\      |
| kap              | numeric | 16      |             | \\\[0, \infty)\\      |
| s                | numeric | 4       |             | \\\[0, \infty)\\      |
| tau_kap          | numeric | 3       |             | \\\[0, \infty)\\      |
| tau_s            | numeric | 0.5     |             | \\\[0, \infty)\\      |
| verbose          | logical | FALSE   | TRUE, FALSE | \-                    |
| update_tau       | logical | TRUE    | TRUE, FALSE | \-                    |
| parallel         | logical | TRUE    | TRUE, FALSE | \-                    |
| random_seed      | integer | \-      |             | \\(-\infty, \infty)\\ |
| sample_weights   | logical | TRUE    | TRUE, FALSE | \-                    |
| nthread          | integer | \-      |             | \\\[0, \infty)\\      |

## References

He, Jingyu, Yalov, Saar, Hahn, Richard P (2019). “XBART: Accelerated
Bayesian Additive Regression Trees.” In *Proceedings of the 22nd
International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Statistics*,
volume 89 series Proceedings of Machine Learning Research, 1130–1138.

He, Jingyu, Hahn, Richard P (2023). “Stochastic Tree Ensembles for
Regularized Nonlinear Regression.” *Journal of the American Statistical
Association*, **118**(541), 551–570.
[doi:10.1080/01621459.2021.1942012](https://doi.org/10.1080/01621459.2021.1942012)
.

## Examples

``` r
# Define the Learner
learner = lrn("regr.xbart")
print(learner)
#> 
#> ── <LearnerRegrXBART> (regr.xbart): Accelerated Bayesian Additive Regression Tre
#> • Model: -
#> • Parameters: num_trees=100, num_sweeps=40, nthread=1
#> • Packages: mlr3, mlr3extralearners, and XBART
#> • Predict Types: [response]
#> • Feature Types: logical, integer, and numeric
#> • Encapsulation: none (fallback: -)
#> • Properties:
#> • Other settings: use_weights = 'error', predict_raw = 'FALSE'

# Define a Task
task = tsk("mtcars")

# Create train and test set
ids = partition(task)

# Train the learner on the training ids
learner$train(task, row_ids = ids$train)

print(learner$model)
```
